text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nine die in communal riots in midwestern Warri oil-producing area.
- Information Minister Walter Ofonagoro says human rights campaign against Nigeria is biased and asks international community to deal with his country on the basis of truth and mutual respect.
- Federal government reviews policy on wholesale liquidation of ailing banks. Sources say some will be axed but those that can be be revived will be saved.
- Central bank may bar 25 banks from participating in the weekly foreign exchange auction for flouting policy on basic travel allowance for Nigerians going abroad.
- Two more villages in troubled Warri area razed, eight feared dead in renewed clashes.
- Nigeria embarks on a project to link it directly with neighbouring countries by telephone rather than routing through former colonial capitals London and Paris.

- Government serves notice to terminate services of import inspection agents Societe Generale de Surveillance and Cotecna International Limited with effect from May 1 and appoints Anglia International Services Limited in their place.
- Central bank orders banks to return unused foreign exchange sold to them at the weekly foreign exchange auction.
- Nigeria has exported petrochemicals products to the United States, Britain, Egypt, The Netherlands, Spain, Belgium, Ghana and India and has orders from South Africa, sources say.
